target_customer: Academic and commercial researchers who pay to recruit vetted online participants, later AI labs buying human data and evaluations
problem: Researchers struggled to find reliable, genuine and diverse online participants, especially outside the US where Mechanical Turk was limited.
business_model: Marketplace: researchers pay participant rewards plus a platform fee on each study
product_category: Participant recruitment and human data marketplace

founders.name: Phelim Bradley
education: PhD in bioinformatics, University of Oxford
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as co-founder and CEO with a bioinformatics PhD; TechCrunch 2019 says he was a doctoral student at Oxford in 2014. Role details from a search summary of company coverage.

founders.name: Ekaterina Damer
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch (2019-12-04) as co-founder; she conceived the idea while struggling to recruit participants for her PhD. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Amazon Mechanical Turk
competitors.what: Crowdsourcing marketplace most researchers used for online studies

competitors.name: CloudResearch
competitors.what: Research layer built on the MTurk API

competitors.name: Positly
competitors.what: Research layer built on the MTurk API

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed participant vetting, fraud screening, pre-screening filters and payments at scale; standard engineering with hard quality problems.

defensibility.rationale: Two sided marketplace with a vetted pool of 70,000 participants in 2019 and rich pre-screening data; rivals were big panels or thin MTurk wrappers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it quickly or bought it; Prolific stayed independent, bootstrapped to profitability in 2020 per its own press release.

market_need_then: Researchers reported poor quality and US-only limits on MTurk; the 2017 Oxford release cites a paper finding Prolific participants less dishonest and more diverse than MTurk. TechCrunch 2019 reports over 3,000 customers mostly by word of mouth.

branding.name_origin: Originally Prolific Academic, a descriptive label for a research platform; the shorter Prolific was in use by March 2017 per an Oxford University Innovation release. Reason for the change not found.
branding.domain_note: Earlier used prolific.ac and prolific.co; now prolific.com (domain history dates not found).

identity.logo: Redesigned logo, colours and font in 2023 per the company's rebrand post
identity.voice_and_tone: Ethical, quality focused, fair pay for participants

branding.brand_signature: Fair pay and ethical treatment of participants

rebrands.why: Company says it wanted to show commitment to ethical methods and quality as it grew

branding.community_and_virality: Went viral on TikTok in a data quality episode that the company wrote about; academia knows it by word of mouth.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among academic researchers, reputation for ethics and quality, but not a consumer brand.

pivots.from: Academic and market research participant recruitment
pivots.to: Also human data and evaluation for AI training
pivots.why: Funding announcement says it would broaden AI offerings; demand for human feedback on models

outcome_analysis: Prolific grew by word of mouth among academic researchers as a higher quality alternative to MTurk, reached profitability in 2020 after a small 2019 seed, and then raised a 25M pound (about 32M dollar) round in July 2023 as AI labs began buying human data. It has about 180 people. A viral sample quality episode shows reputational risk but no shutdown or exit.
notes: Series A amount: company says 25M pounds, outlets report about 32M dollars; recorded as 32M dollars from the reported conversion. Sacra estimates 1.4M seed, TechCrunch says 1.2M, TechCrunch used. Company says bootstrapped and no earlier round stated. Series A lead investors from the company release; Partech and OSE confirmed by tech.eu and Silicon Angle via search results.
